categories.main_business_segments: Winner Medical Co., Ltd. operates primarily in two segments: medical consumables and consumer products. The medical segment includes wound care, infection protection, surgical consumables, personal and family healthcare products. The consumer segment, under the Purcotton brand, offers cotton-based products such as cotton soft towels, sanitary napkins, baby and adult apparel, and home textiles.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes innovation in core materials, including proprietary development of high-end dressings, PC substrates, and radiation protection clothing. It pioneered the patented all-cotton spunlace nonwoven fabric technology for consumer products. Manufacturing integrates intelligent and green production methods, including advanced equipment, photovoltaic power, and heat recovery to enhance efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include hospitals, healthcare providers, retail pharmacies, and end consumers seeking high-quality medical and cotton-based consumer products. The company serves both domestic Chinese markets and over 110 countries internationally, with a focus on medical institutions and consumers valuing safety, comfort, and environmental sustainability.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations span multiple regions in China including Wuhan, Shenzhen, Hubei, Guangxi, Zhejiang, and Hunan provinces, as well as international locations such as the United States, Vietnam, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, and other global markets. The company has production facilities and sales channels across these regions, supporting a global supply chain and market presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: Winner Medical operates across the supply chain from upstream raw material procurement and core material R&D to midstream manufacturing and downstream sales and distribution. It controls a full industry chain for medical consumables and cotton consumer products, including OEM, ODM, and proprietary brand sales.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes product leadership through continuous innovation in core materials and product upgrades, including biomedical and tissue engineering research. It focuses on digital transformation, intelligent manufacturing, and green development. R&D efforts include developing advanced wound dressings, cotton tech innovations, and bio-materials like collagen extraction for artificial corneas.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through product sales of medical consumables and consumer cotton products. Sales channels include direct sales to hospitals, retail pharmacies, online e-commerce platforms, and offline brand stores. The company also engages in OEM and ODM manufacturing for global clients.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Winner Medical is positioned as a leading domestic and international brand in low-value medical consumables and cotton consumer products. It competes with global medical device manufacturers and domestic textile and healthcare product companies, leveraging its integrated supply chain, innovation capabilities, and brand reputation to maintain competitive advantages.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the company achieved approximately RMB 8.98 billion in revenue, a 9.7% increase year-over-year, with net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 695 million, up 19.8%. The company has shown steady growth driven by both organic development and strategic acquisitions, including the purchase of the US-based GRI company to expand global capacity.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Winner Medical emphasizes quality over profit, brand over speed, and social value over corporate value. Its unique value lies in medical-grade cotton technology, high-quality and safe medical consumables, and environmentally friendly products. The company differentiates through proprietary technologies, rigorous quality control, comprehensive product portfolios, and strong brand equity in both medical and consumer markets.
